newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urged to explain U.S. policy on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urged to explain U.S. policy on Iraq.

text.p: House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich, stepping up Republican pressure on the White House over Iraq, said on Monday President Bill Clinton should give Americans a clear explanation of U.S. policy.

The Georgia Republican accused the Clinton administration of causing a diplomatic misstep over the planned deployment of U.S. troops from Texas to Kuwait, calling it evidence of an overly eager White House public relations campaign.

"We can't even get the ally we're defending to agree to be defended before we issue the press release saying we're going to be defending them. It tells you there's a certain lack of coordination. This should not be a public relations campaign," Gingrich told reporters.
"The president owes the country a clear explanation of what he is doing, why he is doing it and what does he hope to accomplish."

Clinton ordered 44 cruise missiles fired at air defence targets in southern Iraq in back-to-back strikes this month to punish Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein for sending troops into a Western-protected enclave in northern Iraq to back a faction in inter-Kurdish fighting.

The Pentagon on Sunday delayed a possible deployment of up to 5,000 additional Army troops to join a U.S. buildup in and around the Gulf region, apparently because of Kuwaiti qualms about hosting them.

Earlier on Monday Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole criticised U.S. strategy on ABC's "Good Morning America" programme, saying it used million-dollar missiles to damage $60,000 Iraqi radar installations.

Gingrich said the attacks were not only costly but used a weapon the Clinton administration would rather not replace. "It takes you 18 months to build a cruise missile and President Clinton says he doesn't want any. They're firing out of a very limited inventory they don't want to replace.

"They ought to slow down the publicity campaign and speed up the diplomatic campaign. And then they ought to ask the military: What's the purpose of this? You make a big bang with a missile but what do you accomplish?" Gingrich said.
